Can Lifting Clothes, Per Se, Amount to Attempt to Rape?

The judgment of the Jharkhand High Court has once again created a hue and cry among many individuals, as the High Court held that the act of lifting the clothes, per se, would not amount to an attempt to rape.

My view may be somewhat controversial, but in my opinion, the reasoning adopted by the High Court was correct. In the present case, as per the deposition of the prosecutrix, the offender had lifted her clothes and attempted to commit rape. However, the victim failed to depose about the exact nature of the act attributable to the offender. The statement that the accused “attempted to commit rape” is an extremely vague and bald allegation, as the victim was required to depose about the exact nature of the act. Unless the nature of such act is specifically deposed to, the Court cannot presume that the act amounted to an attempt to rape.

An attempt to rape requires the act to have a close proximity to the commission of rape, along with some overt act indicating an attempt to penetrate. The Supreme Court, in Ishwar Chand Sharma v. State of U.P., SLP (Crl.) No. 18035 of 2025, held that the victim should state the exact nature of the act committed upon her, and that bald allegations of rape are insufficient. The same analogy, in my view, would apply to cases involving an alleged attempt to rape. However, in the present case, the victim failed to depose about the exact act committed by the accused and merely stated that there was an “attempt to rape,” without anything further.

It is pertinent to note that the mere act of lifting a woman’s clothes, without any overt act towards penetration, is not sufficient to hold an accused guilty of an attempt to rape. Where only the clothes are lifted, without any overt act towards penetration, the accused can argue that his intention was merely to disrobe the woman and not to commit rape as no specific act of pointing towards penetration is attributable. Such an act of disrobing may instead attract Section 354B of the IPC / Section 76 of the BNS.

The reliance placed on the Supreme Court’s judgment in In Re: Order Dated 17.03.2025 Passed by the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad is also, in my view, misplaced, as the Supreme Court, in that judgment, failed to appreciate the true import of the concept of “attempt” and the scope of Section 354B IPC.
